slides.title: Solving Tech Problems
slides.content:
1. Common Problems

  • The screen is frozen: It doesn't move.
  • I can't log in: My password is not working.
  • The Wi-Fi is down: No internet connection.
  • The printer is jammed: Paper is stuck inside.

2. Giving Instructions (Imperatives)

To give technical help, use the verb directly:

Restart the computer.
Click on the icon.
Check the cable.
Don't turn off the power.
slides.speech_text: Don't panic when technology fails. First, describe the problem: 'My screen is frozen'. Then, follow instructions. We use imperatives like 'Restart', 'Click', or 'Open' to tell someone what to do.

slides.title: Help Desk Call
slides.content: Listen to an employee calling IT support.
slides.audio_script:
IT Support: IT Help Desk, this is Kevin. How can I help?
        Employee: Hi Kevin. I have a problem. I can't access my email.
        IT Support: Okay. Is there an error message?
        Employee: Yes, it says 'Incorrect Password', but I am using the right one.
        IT Support: I see. Please click on 'Forgot Password' and check your phone for a code.
        Employee: Ah, okay. I see the code now. Thanks!

quiz.question: What does Kevin tell the employee to do?

slides.title: Fix it!
slides.instruction: Select the correct instruction for each problem.

questions.text: Problem: The computer is very slow. Solution: ____ it.
questions.explanation: Para dar instrucciones usamos el Imperativo (el verbo en su forma base).

questions.text: Problem: No internet. Solution: ____ the router cable.
Problem: The file is closed. Solution: ____ it again.

slides.title: Roleplay: IT Assistant
slides.system_prompt:
You are an IT Support Specialist.
        The user is a colleague with a technical problem.
        
        Steps:
        1. Ask: "Hello, IT Support. What is the problem?"
        2. Listen to their issue (e.g., printer not working, no internet).
        3. Give them a simple instruction using an IMPERATIVE (e.g., "Restart the router", "Check the cable").
        4. Ask if it works now.
        
        Correction Focus: If the user describes the problem vaguely ("It's bad"), ask for details ("Is there an error message?").
slides.initial_message: IT Support here. What seems to be the problem with your computer?
slides.user_goal: Describe a problem (e.g., 'My internet is slow') and follow the instruction.
